answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so influence decays across sparse boundaries rather than compounding unchecked. A Sybil cluster is glacier-like: its low-conductance external cut limits escape probability and, under min-cut transitivity bounds, caps aggregate voting weight. Thus, even a spiral of mutually attesting identities cannot become a trust haven without credible links to the honest graph.
